places.name: Musee Marmottan Monet
places.connection: Permanent home since 1940-world's largest Monet collection

places.name: Port of Le Havre
places.connection: The location depicted in the painting. Monet painted it from a hotel room overlooking the port.

places.name: Nadar's Studio (former location)
places.connection: Site of the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874, where 'Impression, Sunrise' was first displayed.

places.name: National Gallery
places.connection: Monet and Pissarro visited London in 1870-71, where they studied the works of J.M.W. Turner and John Constable, which heavily influenced their approach to light and atmosphere.

places.name: La Ferme Saint-Siméon
places.connection: An inn that served as a meeting place for the Honfleur School, where Monet, Boudin, and Jongkind gathered and developed their plein air techniques.

places.name: Hôtel Drouot
places.connection: The auction house where the painting was sold in 1878 for only 210 francs after its first owner, Ernest Hoschedé, went bankrupt.

places.name: Port of Le Havre
places.connection: The location depicted in the painting, Monet's hometown.

places.name: Boulevard des Capucines
places.connection: Location of the first Impressionist Exhibition in 1874, where this painting was first shown.
